focus: Review the PU-018 trace plan and slice spec for product-contract contradictions, incorrect stage ownership, heading-shape ambiguity, and KnowledgeOS boundary leakage.
result_json: {"status":"findings","summary":"Found contract-boundary issues that could let the next execution plan collapse stage ownership or implement an incomplete governed-stage validator: slice-spec acceptance depends on a future execution-plan artifact, source-context validator markers omit required claim/freshness/budget fields, required agent metadata lacks acceptance coverage, and the exact H2 contract does not state whether extra H2 headings are forbidden.","findings":[{"severity":"major","file":".harness/specs/2026-06-11-skills-sdk-pu-018-compact-stage-skill-shape-spec.md","line":176,"issue":"Acceptance criterion 1 says the PU-018 execution plan must exist, but this slice spec's own exit condition says the spec is complete when it exists and hands off only to execution-plan. That makes slice-spec acceptance depend on a future-stage artifact and blurs tracker/spec/execution ownership.","recommendation":"Move execution-plan existence out of the slice-spec acceptance criteria, or reword it as a handoff requirement for the next stage. Keep spec acceptance limited to defining the product contract, boundaries, non-goals, and validation expectations."},{"severity":"major","file":".harness/specs/2026-06-11-skills-sdk-pu-018-compact-stage-skill-shape-spec.md","line":103,"issue":"The source-context contract says the file must include only schema_version, skill, stage, template, original_references, load_when, and provenance_policy as required markers, while line 115 says source-context must map allowed claims, forbidden claims, freshness, and context budget. The acceptance criteria later only require source/provenance markers, so an implementation could omit the claim and budget controls and still appear compliant.","recommendation":"Make the required source-context schema explicit enough for validation: include markers or nested fields for reference index entries, allowed_claims, forbidden_claims, freshness, and context_budget, or state precisely which companion file owns each of those controls."},{"severity":"major","file":".harness/specs/2026-06-11-skills-sdk-pu-018-compact-stage-skill-shape-spec.md","line":72,"issue":"The product contract requires agent execution metadata and lists agents/openai.yaml as a required companion file, but the requirements and acceptance criteria do not explicitly require validation of agents/openai.yaml. The execution plan could validate only SKILL.md and references files, leaving the agent execution metadata unimplemented.","recommendation":"Add a requirement and acceptance criterion that the validator/scaffold enforce agents/openai.yaml presence and required fields, or explicitly defer agent metadata validation to another slice if PU-018 should only scaffold it."},{"severity":"minor","file":".harness/specs/2026-06-11-skills-sdk-pu-018-compact-stage-skill-shape-spec.md","line":58,"issue":"The spec requires an exact H2 heading order but does not say whether these are the complete set of allowed H2 headings, whether case/punctuation must match exactly, or whether additional H2 headings are rejected. That ambiguity matters because the old 17-heading shape could survive as extra H2s while the compact headings appear in order.","recommendation":"Define the heading contract as an exact ordered set of H2 headings, including case-sensitive display text or normalized slug rules, and state whether additional H2 headings are forbidden for governed SDK stage skills."}]}

focus: Review the PU-018 trace plan and slice spec for missing implementation acceptance criteria, validator/scaffold/test migration gaps, and ambiguous proof commands.
result_json: {"status":"findings","summary":"The PU-018 trace plan and slice spec capture the compact-stage intent, but several acceptance criteria are still too loose for implementation: companion governance schemas can be satisfied by presence-only files, source-context claim/freshness/budget requirements are not made enforceable, the reference-unit validator is underspecified, and migration/proof scope is not tied to a deterministic inventory command.","findings":[{"severity":"major","file":".harness/specs/2026-06-11-skills-sdk-pu-018-compact-stage-skill-shape-spec.md","line":72,"issue":"Required companion files are listed by path, but the spec never defines required schemas or minimum keys for references/contract.yaml, references/evals.yaml, references/task-profile.json, or agents/openai.yaml. Later requirements only say the validator must require the files, so an implementation could create empty or shallow companion files and still appear compliant.","recommendation":"Add implementation acceptance criteria for each companion file: required top-level keys, required governance concepts, and validator/scaffold fixtures proving missing or empty governance files fail."},{"severity":"major","file":".harness/specs/2026-06-11-skills-sdk-pu-018-compact-stage-skill-shape-spec.md","line":103,"issue":"The Source Context Contract lists only seven marker keys, while the same paragraph says source-context must map allowed claims, forbidden claims, freshness, and context budget. Acceptance criterion 6 later only requires source/provenance markers, leaving the stricter claim/freshness/budget contract unenforced.","recommendation":"Promote allowed claims, forbidden claims, freshness, context budget, and reference index entries into explicit required source-context fields, then require positive and negative validator tests for those fields."},{"severity":"major","file":".harness/specs/2026-06-11-skills-sdk-pu-018-compact-stage-skill-shape-spec.md","line":160,"issue":"The reference-unit rule says Markdown references must be bounded to one viewpoint, evidence lane, runbook, rubric, prior-art source, or substantial context unit, but it does not define how validation should determine that without brittle content heuristics. The trace plan explicitly warns against naive word-count checks, so the implementation path is ambiguous.","recommendation":"Define the validator mechanism before execution, such as source-context metadata declaring reference kind, authority/provenance, claim scope, and allowed combinations, plus fixtures for focused references, composite runbooks that are allowed, mixed dossiers that fail, and upstream exports that remain out of scope."},{"severity":"major","file":".harness/specs/2026-06-11-skills-sdk-pu-018-compact-stage-skill-shape-spec.md","line":166,"issue":"Migration acceptance requires every existing governed SDK stage skill to pass after migration, but the spec does not require a deterministic inventory command or captured list of the skills being migrated. The trace plan mentions 12 current SDK stage skills, but neither artifact makes the migration set a proof artifact.","recommendation":"Require the execution plan to discover and record the governed-stage inventory with an exact command before edits, use that inventory as the migration checklist, and prove after migration that the same discovered set passes the updated validator."},{"severity":"minor","file":".harness/specs/2026-06-11-skills-sdk-pu-018-compact-stage-skill-shape-spec.md","line":195,"issue":"The validation plan includes concrete narrow commands, but the widening rule says to add the relevant repo wrapper before closeout without naming which wrapper or when it becomes mandatory. That leaves proof expectations ambiguous for changes touching broader authoring validators or repo status surfaces.","recommendation":"Name the expected closeout wrapper or decision rule explicitly, for example require the execution plan to run the documented repo closeout or authoring-family wrapper when validator/scaffold behavior changes, and report blocked with a reason if it cannot run."}]}

focus: Review the PU-018 trace plan and slice spec for evidence-lane overclaims, unverified assumptions, PR/CI/review readiness leakage, and reference/KnowledgeOS validation risk.
